label: Reconstructed 1812 working woman's dress (a short gown of a madder print with elbow sleeves and a skirt to the hip over a blue homespun petticoat to the ankle, a broad natural linen apron tied at the waist, a white kerchief round the neck, a plain linen cap, shoes) and its woman-of-the-country variant (the short gown a red calico, the petticoat dark stroud, a blue cotton handkerchief wrapped round the head, moccasins) on the shared portable female rig
basis: The T-3423 bodice loosened and cut back to the elbow as a short gown, its skirt lofted outside the petticoat to the hip, a petticoat lofted round the body's own sections to the ankle, a broad apron laid over both and hung straight, its band round the waist, a kerchief shell round the neck, a cap or a handkerchief laid over the hair, and the shared closed shoe (as shoes or moccasins), after Wau-Bun's Chicago woman of 1812, Lambert and Krimmel (tools/human_women_1812.py, T-3464). Every amount and colour is reconstructed.
source_scope: Wau-Bun (1856; the Kinzie family's narrative) gives Mrs Helm's disguise on 16 August 1812 as 'the ordinary dress of a Frenchwoman of the country; namely, a short gown and petticoat, with a blue cotton handkerchief wrapped around her head'; Lambert (1810, Lower Canada 1806-08) that 'A petticoat and short jacket, is the most prevailing dress', with muslin aprons, handkerchiefs and full caps, and moccasins among the country people; Krimmel's Philadelphia woman of 1811-13 (Met) a head-wrap, a short gown and a striped petticoat; the Met's 1810-20 cap the close shape. None shows a soldier's wife, a laundress or a French woman at Chicago.

women_components.evidence_choice: The brief asked for a soldier's wife or laundress and a French woman of the country in Wau-Bun's short gown and petticoat, with an apron, a kerchief and either a linen cap or the blue cotton handkerchief. Both heads are built: the cap on woman_working_1812 (the laundresses, the settlers' wives and the Healds' servant Cicely, T-3464 day.json), the handkerchief on the variant woman_country_1812 (Archange Ouilmette, Mrs Bisson, Josette LaFramboise), which also takes the woman of the country's red print, dark stroud and moccasins; it costs a whole asset of bytes and the integrator may drop it. The sleeves end below the elbow, the working length of T-3464's reading; the petticoat is not kilted up.

provenance.source_scope: A short gown (a loose jacket-bodice, here with elbow sleeves and a skirt to the hip): Wau-Bun's 'short gown and petticoat' at Chicago in 1812, Lambert's 'petticoat and short jacket', Krimmel's working woman of 1811-13. The ease, the sleeve length (T-3464 day.json: elbow or three-quarter), the hip length and the madder print drawn as its mean colour are reconstructed.

A petticoat to the ankle under the short gown (the same three). Blue homespun is one of T-3464 day.json's colours (striped, blue, brown or madder); the stripe of Krimmel's is drawn as a plain colour; the fullness and the hem's height, just clear of the ankle, are reconstructed.

An apron round the front and sides, tied at the waist over the short gown: Lambert names aprons; T-3464 day.json reads a coarse linen or checked apron. Natural linen, its breadth and length are reconstructed.
A kerchief round the neck (Lambert's 'handkerchiefs'; T-3464 day.json); white, its fold and depth reconstructed.
A plain linen cap over the hair (Lambert's caps; the Met's 1810-20 cap for the close shape, a lady's, made plainer here with a narrow frill). Reconstructed.
Heavy shoes (T-3464 day.json: stockings and heavy shoes, or bare feet at the washing); the shared closed shoe; reconstructed.
The woman of the country's short gown (Wau-Bun, Chicago 1812); a red printed calico (T-3464 day.json: red, blue or brown print) drawn as its mean colour is reconstructed.
Her petticoat (Wau-Bun, Chicago 1812); dark blue stroud (T-3464 day.json: dark blue or black stroud or homespun; Wau-Bun names strouding among the trade goods) is reconstructed.

'a blue cotton handkerchief wrapped around her head' (Wau-Bun, of a French woman of the country at Chicago, 16 August 1812): graded inferred, not attested, because the source is the Kinzie family's narrative of 1856; how it is wrapped, the knot at the nape and the shade of blue are reconstructed.

Moccasins: Lambert's moccasins 'in general use among the country people', and Wau-Bun's engage's moccasins at Chicago in 1812. The shared closed shoe stands for them in a smoked-leather colour; their cut is not modelled.
